findings.title: U1 pin EN is floating / undriven
findings.failure_mode: A floating EN/CHIP_PU leaves the module in an indeterminate reset state — unreliable or no boot.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet + hardware design guidelines: EN (CHIP_PU) must be pulled up (typ. 10k) with a delay cap; it must not float or the module may not boot reliably.

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 100n
findings.failure_mode: A 1uF (instead of 100nF) cap on IO0 defeats the auto-download/reset sequence — can't flash without manual BOOT.
findings.citation: ESP32 auto-program circuit: IO0 uses a 100nF cap. A 1uF cap here (as on EN) is too large and breaks the auto-download timing.

findings.title: DevKit fed on both 5V and 3V3 pins; its onboard LDO output is paralleled with U16 through R31 (0 Ω)
findings.detail: U1 pin 21 (5V) sits on +5V (LM7805 U3 output and AP2112 U16 input). U1 pins 1 and 2 (3V3) go through R31 (0 Ω) to the board's +3.3V rail, which U16 drives. The DevKit has its own 3.3 V LDO powered from its 5V pin, so its 3V3 pins are a regulator output. That puts the DevKit LDO and U16 directly in parallel. The datasheet says the 5V pin and the 3V3 pin are mutually exclusive ways to power the board. Also, when USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5 V is tied to the 5V pin and drives back into the LM7805 output.
findings.failure_mode: Two LDOs on one rail fight each other and share current unpredictably, so one of them may end up carrying the whole load. With USB connected while the board is powered (for example during programming), USB 5 V and the 7805 output are tied together and can backfeed the host or the regulator. Fix: leave R31 unpopulated and let each side regulate its own 3.3 V, or power the DevKit through only one pin.

findings.title: ILI9341 module datasheet not available; DS1 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet could be found for DS1 (an ILI9341 TFT module with a touch controller), so its pin connections could not be checked against the manufacturer's specifications. In the netlist, VCC is on +3.3V. The display and touch controller share SCK and MOSI on GPIO4 and GPIO5, with separate chip selects on GPIO7 and GPIO18. The backlight pin LED is driven directly by GPIO17. SDO(MISO) is left unconnected.
findings.failure_mode: Without the module datasheet, nobody can confirm that 3.3 V VCC is correct for this module. Nobody can confirm either that GPIO17 can drive the LED pin directly without a transistor on the module.

findings.title: TS5A23157 datasheet unavailable; SW3 not verified
findings.detail: No datasheet for the TS5A23157 (SW3) could be found, so its pinout, logic thresholds and supply rating could not be checked against the netlist. Topology: IN1 and IN2 are driven by GPIO21 and GPIO47, V+ is on +3.3V, and the COM pins take the AD9833 outputs. Note that the footprint is a module (ohmen:TS5A23157_Module), so the pin numbering must match the breakout board, not the bare IC.
findings.failure_mode: If the module pin mapping doesn't match the symbol, the signal routing or power connections could be wrong.

findings.title: U1 pin EN has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing EN pull-up => no defined power-on reset delay.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: EN uses a ~10k pull-up to 3V3 plus a 1uF delay cap (RC reset).

findings.title: U1 pin IO0 has no net for a required 10k
findings.failure_mode: Missing IO0 pull-up can leave the module entering download mode unexpectedly.
findings.citation: ESP32-S3 hardware design guidelines: IO0 (boot strap) needs a pull-up (typ. 10k) so the module boots to flash by default.

dropped.title: TEC2-1221WI is a ±5 V module, but it feeds the ±12 V rails
dropped.detail: U2 is a TEC 2-1221WI. The datasheet lists that order code as a +5 VDC / –5 VDC, 200 mA output. Its outputs drive the nets +12V (pin 6) and -12V (pin 8), which supply the OPA2810 op-amps (U10, U11, U12 and others). Those rails are designed for ±12 V. The ±12 V part in the same family is the TEC 2-1222WI (83 mA per output). Either the part number or the rail names are wrong.
dropped.failure_mode: With this part fitted, the op-amp stages get only ±5 V instead of ±12 V. Output swing and headroom fall far short of the design, so the analog signals will clip.

dropped.title: U16 input capacitors C2/C32 have no value
dropped.detail: The only capacitors on U16's VIN rail (+5V) are C2 and C32. Both are generic 'C_Small_US' symbols with no capacitance value. The datasheet's typical circuit asks for a 1µF ceramic CIN (X5R/X7R). The output side is fine because it has several 10µF and 100nF capacitors.
dropped.failure_mode: If the input capacitance is missing, too small, or not near U16, the LDO can ring or drop out during load steps from the ESP32 and display, especially since +5V also comes from the LM7805 output.
dropped.excerpt: It is recommended to use X7R or X5R dielectric capacitor if 1.0 µF ceramic capacitor is selected as input/output capacitors.

dropped.title: DevKit fed through both the 5V and 3V3 pins at once, which the datasheet says are mutually exclusive
dropped.detail: U1 pin 21 (5V) is on +5V, which the LM7805 (U3) drives. U1 pins 1 and 2 (3V3) go through the 0 Ω resistor R31 to +3.3V, which the AP2112K (U16) drives. That puts the DevKit's own on-board 3.3 V LDO output in parallel with U16's output. When USB is plugged in, the DevKit's USB 5 V can also feed back onto the +5V rail. The DevKit guide lists 5V and 3V3 as two of three mutually exclusive ways to power the board.
dropped.failure_mode: Two LDOs with paralleled outputs fight over the rail and share load unpredictably, and one can reverse-bias the other. A USB connection can back-drive the 7805 output and the analog 5 V rail. Pick one supply path: either leave R31 unfitted and use the DevKit's 3V3 as an output, or stop feeding the 5V pin.

dropped.title: VREF/RFB driven by op-amps on ±12V rails, equal to the ±12V absolute maximum
dropped.detail: U8 VREF (pin 7) is driven directly by U4 OUT (gained_func), and RFB (pin 8) by U5 OUT; both OPA2810s are powered from +12V/-12V. The AD5452 absolute maximum for VREF and RFB is ±12V, so there is no margin: any rail tolerance above 12V, or a saturated or overdriven gain stage, can put these pins at or past the limit.
dropped.failure_mode: If the gain stage saturates (from too much input gain or at power-up) while the rails are slightly high, VREF/RFB can go beyond ±12V and damage the DAC's R-2R ladder. Limit the signal swing to the ±10V operating range or add clamping.
dropped.excerpt: VREF, RFB to GND −12 V to +12 V

dropped.title: ILI9341 module datasheet unavailable; DS1 connections not verified
dropped.detail: There is no datasheet for DS1 (ILI9341 TFT module), so its pinout could not be checked against a source. Two netlist facts need an engineer to review them. First, SDO(MISO) on pin 9 is not connected, so the MCU can never read from the display. Second, the touch controller's T_DOUT goes to its own GPIO6 instead of sharing a MISO line. Pin 8 (LED) is driven straight from GPIO17. Whether that is safe depends on whether the module has its own backlight transistor or resistor.
dropped.failure_mode: If the module has no backlight driver, GPIO17 might be overloaded by the backlight current. The pin assignments also cannot be confirmed without the datasheet.
